headline: Calcutta HC admits Customs appeal on special warehouse licence eligibility after penalty
reference: Principal Commissioner of Customs (Airport & A.C.C), Kolkata vs M/s Nuance Group (India) Pvt Ltd, CUSTA/114/2026, Calcutta High Court, order dated 25 November 2026
summary_points: Calcutta HC admitted the Revenue's customs appeal on a substantial question of law; this is an admission order, not a final ruling.
Issue: whether a penalty under Section 112 or 114 of the Customs Act makes an applicant 'penalized' under Regulation 2(c) of the Special Warehouse Licensing Regulations, 2016.
The question also turns on Section 58A of the Customs Act and Section 3(38) of the General Clauses Act, and on whether such a person is ineligible for a special warehousing licence.
Paper books and other formalities were dispensed with; the matter will be heard on the existing stay application papers.
The matter is listed 'To be Mentioned' on 26 November 2026, and both sides are to file written notes.
who_is_affected: Importers and warehouse operators applying for special warehousing licences under Section 58A of the Customs Act who have faced customs penalties.
action_required: Track the final outcome of this appeal before relying on any penalty history for licence eligibility, and review pending or planned special warehouse applications accordingly.

social.linkedin:
Calcutta High Court has admitted a Customs appeal that could clarify who is eligible for a special warehousing licence.

In Principal Commissioner of Customs (Airport & A.C.C), Kolkata vs M/s Nuance Group (India) Pvt Ltd, the Division Bench admitted the appeal on a substantial question of law on 25 November 2026.

The question: does a penalty under Section 112 or 114 of the Customs Act mean the applicant has been 'penalized' under Regulation 2(c) of the Special Warehouse Licensing Regulations, 2016, making the applicant ineligible under Section 58A of the Customs Act?

The Court dispensed with paper books and other formalities, and will hear the matter on the existing papers. It is listed 'To be Mentioned' on 26 November 2026, and both sides are to file written notes.

This is only an admission order. There is no ruling on the merits yet, but the outcome could affect importers and warehouse operators with a penalty history.

Please verify with the official order before relying on it.
